title: Fix send-on-closed-channel panic in gateway enqueueWSEvent
description:
**Bug**: `enqueueWSEvent()` at `core/controlplane/gateway/gateway.go:805-813` sends on `s.eventsCh` which can be closed by `stopBusTaps()` at line 138-143. The `select/default` prevents blocking but does NOT prevent panic on a closed channel.

**Fix approach**: Add an atomic flag (e.g. `s.eventsStopped atomic.Bool`) checked before the send, or use a mutex-guarded send pattern. Alternatively, use recover() in the select case, though atomic flag is cleaner.

**Files**: `core/controlplane/gateway/gateway.go`
definitionOfDone: enqueueWSEvent cannot panic when eventsCh is closed
Concurrent test proving no panic under stop+send race

implementationPlan.description: Add `eventsStopped atomic.Bool` field to the `server` struct in gateway.go. This flag will be set to `true` when `stopBusTaps()` is called, before the channel is closed.

Modify `stopBusTaps()` to set `s.eventsStopped.Store(true)` BEFORE closing the channel inside the `sync.Once` block. This ensures the atomic flag is visible to all goroutines before the close happens.

Write a concurrent regression test in gateway_test.go that:
1. Creates a server with an eventsCh
2. Spawns N goroutines calling enqueueWSEvent in a loop
3. Calls stopBusTaps() concurrently
4. Asserts no panic occurs (test passes = no panic)
5. Run with `-race` flag to detect data races
